name: Plexus (Agent Mesh)
description: Plexus — Agent Mesh Protocol v1.3. The frame agents run on: durable MQTT transport, capability discovery, agent-to-agent delegation with lineage and hop limits, and an operator console. Capabilities are data, not code.

url.description: MQTT broker URL (e.g. mqtt://localhost:1883 or mqtts://broker.emqx.io:8883)

clientId.description: MQTT client ID. MUST be stable across restarts or the persistent session (clean:false) is defeated and messages queued while offline are lost. Defaults to openclaw-mqtt-bridge-<hash of host+install path>. Set explicitly only if you run two gateways from the same install directory.

protocolVersion.description: 4 = MQTT 3.1.1 (default, widest broker compatibility). 5 = MQTT 5, which adds a bounded session expiry so decommissioned deployments stop accumulating queued messages.

sessionExpirySeconds.description: MQTT 5 only: how long the broker retains our queued messages while disconnected.

agentId.description: This agent's id within the mesh.

servicesFile.description: Path to the capability catalog. Defaults to services.json beside the plugin. Watched via fs.watch; edits republish the retained profile.

requireOwner.description: Reject invokes with no requestedBy, as protocol 1.2 requires, instead of silently routing them to owner "public". Set false to accept unowned invokes with a warning.

verifyOwner.description: Verify requestedBy against a broker-injected client_username (EMQX rule-engine payload enrichment). Fails closed: with this on, an invoke lacking client_username is rejected. Requires broker-side setup first.

ownerInTopic.description: Protocol 1.4: whether to serve commands/<agentId>/invoke/<owner>, where the owner is in the topic so a broker ACL can enforce who a requester claims to be. "accept" serves both forms and takes the owner from the topic when it is there; "off" serves the 1.3 form only. There is deliberately no mode that refuses the old form: refusing is enforcement, and enforcement belongs to the broker.

feedback.description: Protocol 1.5: whether to serve commands/<agentId>/feedback/<owner>, where a requester says what the work was worth. Off unless somebody states otherwise, and not as a licence check: a verdict is only worth recording where the broker vouches for who is speaking. On a broker with no rules any connected client can file one in anybody's name, and this agent cannot tell — so accepting them would let anyone on the broker decide what the mesh believes about work they had nothing to do with. `plexus-server add-agent` writes "accept" here because at that moment it knows exactly which rules it granted. Set it by hand only if you applied the equivalent rules by hand.

ownerEnforced.description: Whether the broker enforces who a requester may claim to be, reported to clients as ownerPolicy.verified. An agent cannot observe this, so it is stated by whoever applied the broker's rules — plexus-server add-agent --owner-in-topic writes it into the config it generates. Setting it by hand on a broker that does not enforce advertises a guarantee nobody made.

maxJobDurationMs.description: Hard wall-clock cap per job before the mesh publishes a terminal timeout error.

promptVars.description: Deployment values substituted into ${VAR} placeholders in capability prompts, so the same services.json runs in every deployment. Checked before process.env. Use for non-secret identifiers (Slack ids, channel names, repo paths); keep real secrets in the environment. Resolved only at dispatch, never in the retained profile.

maxDepth.description: How many delegation hops a request may travel (A asks B asks C = depth 2). Bounds runaway fan-out and A→B→A cycles. A request arriving deeper is rejected before any work starts.

askTimeoutMs.description: How long mesh_ask waits for a peer's terminal result before giving up, so a delegating agent never hangs on a peer that is offline or overloaded.

delegation.description: Which forms of agent-to-agent delegation are permitted. 'declared' performs only what a capability lists in its delegates[], before the executor starts — deterministic, needs no tool. 'dynamic' allows the executor to call mesh_ask mid-job — flexible, but depends on it choosing to. 'both' (default) enables each; 'off' disables delegation.

enabled.description: Serve the control panel and HTTP API.

path.description: Base path for the panel and its API.

auth.description: Bearer token required for the panel and API. Accepted as an Authorization header, or as ?token= for the SSE stream (EventSource cannot set headers). Unset means no authentication.

sessionKey.description: Session used by the legacy fallback dispatch path when the subagent runtime is unavailable.
